qualitative.gate_2_reason: Discretionary big-ticket consumer electronics and major appliances with lumpy, multi-year replacement cycles that consumers readily defer during tighter budgets, rather than essential daily staples or entrenched everyday habits.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Rejected - G2 Essential Need). Best Buy's core categories—computing, home theater/TVs, gaming, mobile hardware, and appliances—are big-ticket consumer discretionary durables with highly deferrable replacement cycles, not non-deferrable necessities or high-frequency everyday habits. Post-pandemic normalization drove revenue down ~20% from its ~$52B FY22 peak to $41.5B in FY25 (-2.3% comps) before modest stabilization to $41.7B (+0.5% comps) in FY26 and +1.9%-3.0% FY27 comp guidance. Even beyond Gate 2, reselling commoditized third-party OEM hardware at ~4.2% GAAP operating margins against Amazon, Walmart, Costco, and OEM D2C channels fails the Munger quality bar.
qualitative.evidence: Gate 1 passes on transparent US big-box and omni-channel retail operations (bestbuy.com, Geek Squad, Best Buy Ads, Marketplace) with clear Form 10-K reporting. Gate 2 fails: over the past decade revenue fluctuated in a $39B-$51.8B band—peaking near $52B during pandemic stimulus before sliding to $41,528M in FY25 (ended Feb 1, 2025; enterprise comps -2.3%, Domestic -2.5%, International -0.5%; GAAP operating income $1,262M including Best Buy Health goodwill impairment, adj. ~$1,736M; GAAP net income $927M). In FY26 (ended Jan 31, 2026), revenue stabilized at $41,691M (+0.5% comps; Q4 FY26 comps -0.8% and 20.9% enterprise gross margin), with GAAP operating income ~$1,753M-$1,771M (~4.2% margin) and GAAP net income $1,069M; Domestic gross margin held roughly flat YoY only as services, Best Buy Ads, and Marketplace offset lower product margins. H1 FY27 showed cyclical replacement recovery (Q1 rev $8.94B, +2.0% comps; Q2 rev $9.78B, +4.1% comps, aided by ~$34M IEEPA tariff refund; FY27 guidance raised to $42.3B-$42.8B revenue, +1.9%-3.0% comps, $6.70-$6.90 adj. diluted EPS, ~$750M capex). Balance sheet is net cash (~$1.5B-$1.6B cash vs ~$1,176M total debt at FY26-end) and trailing ROIC sits ~24%-26% (10Y avg ROIC 14.2% in dossier), while management transitions from Corie Barry to Jason Bonfig amid tariff uncertainty and memory component cost inflation ('memory storm').
